title: Interactive cost drilldown prototype - consolidated design review and stakeholder feedback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design an interactive cost drilldown flow in the Redwood Console that lets users start from a high-level cost dashboard and rapidly explore cost-by-model, cost-by-route, and token-level contributors through lightweight on-demand panels and inline filters. The prototype demonstrates microinteractions, animated transitions between summary and detail, and a responsive layout for the cost card grid and timeline. This ticket captures the consolidated design review with PMs, Eng, and Finance stakeholders and synthesizes feedback for handoff to engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype includes at least three drilldown paths: model -> route -> token breakdown
Microinteractions defined for card expand/collapse, timeline scrubbing, and filter chips
Performance implications documented and trade-offs noted for on-demand aggregation vs precomputed endpoints
Design sign-off from PM (Product) and one engineering reviewer for feasibility
Accessibility (keyboard nav + color contrast) checks added to QA checklist
design_notes: Primary affordance is an expandable cost card with lightweight overlay — avoids full route navigation to keep context
Prefers lazy-loading of the token-level table to avoid initial load spikes; placeholder skeletons used during fetch
Timeline scrubbing uses 100ms throttle with visible loading spinner when switching model variants
We propose two layout variants: stacked overlays for narrow viewports, and split-panel drilldown for desktop
Color tokens use semantic palette from Console theme; alternate palette provided for color-blind accessibility
decisions: Use overlay panel pattern rather than full-page navigation to preserve user context (agreed with PM)
Token-level aggregation will be fetched on demand — avoids backend cost spikes; ENG to provide an optimized endpoint or cached materialized view
Keep timeline micro-interaction subtle (ease-in) to prevent distracting users during live scrubbing
Default drilldown entry will be 'model' for new users; advanced users can pin a 'route-first' preference in settings
feedback_summary: PM: prioritize fast first-load for high-level cost dashboard; drilldowns can be async
Engineering: concerned about N+1 requests when multiple cards expanded; suggested batch endpoints or GraphQL field batching (related ENG-2803)
Finance: requested a CSV export option from drilldown views and a clear 'charged-to' column
Design lead: iterate on token-level row density; suggested condensed rows with hover-to-expand for full prompt context
Accessibility reviewer: enforce 4.5:1 contrast on cost delta chips and verify focus order for drilldown overlay
next_steps: Schedule a technical sync with ENG-2803 owners to define batching contract (owner: Omar Reyes) by 2026-03-12
Update Figma prototype with condensed token rows + CSV export affordance by 2026-03-15
Add QA checklist to ticket and assign to QA engineer for pre-release validation (include keyboard nav and CSV tests)
Create a small A/B test plan for overlay vs split-panel in beta release to measure engagement and query load
